entries.title: LLM Providers update: convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages
entries.summary: LLM Providers changes across 1 file(s) (+148/−2).

ai.title: Merge consecutive assistant messages into one wire message
ai.summary: The OpenAI-compatible chat message converter now merges consecutive assistant messages into a single wire message, concatenating `text`, `reasoningContent`, and `toolCalls` in order and unioning provider metadata onto the prior message via `Object.assign`. This addresses thinking models like DeepSeek V4 that require `reasoning_content` to sit on the message carrying `tool_calls`, since a separate adjacent assistant message fails the request. New tests assert merging runs of consecutive assistant messages while preserving separation when another role intervenes.
ai.evidence: In `packages/llm-providers/src/openai-compatible/chat/convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts, the assistant case now checks messages[messages.length - 1]`; when `previous?.role === 'assistant', it appends text`, `reasoningContent`, and `toolCalls to that prior message and calls Object.assign(previous, metadata)` before breaking, instead of pushing a new assistant message.

ai.title: Referral failed and sock-signal analytics events added
ai.summary: Two new `AnalyticsEvent` members were added to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`: `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEM_FAILED = 'freebuff.referral.redeem_failed'` and `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_SOCK_SIGNAL = 'freebuff.referral.sock_signal'`, both placed directly after `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEMED` and before `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_COMPLETED`. Their accompanying comments describe `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEM_FAILED` as a one-shot guard signal for redemption blockers (signup_too_old, user_banned, self_referral, etc.) and `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_SOCK_SIGNAL` as a non-verdict attribution signal that a referred user shares an IP/browser with the referrer, to be weighed by the referral sweep jobs against farming signals. These events extend the server-side referral lifecycle funnel documented in the same enum, but no reader in this diff emits them, so the change seeds telemetry infrastructure rather than shipping tracked behavior.

ai.title: Atomic writes for chat state and corrupt chat listing in /history
ai.summary: A new `writeFileAtomic` utility in `cli/src/utils/write-file-atomic.ts` replaces the plain `fs.writeFileSync` calls in `run-state-storage.ts`'s `saveChatState`, writing `run-state.json` and `chat-messages.json` atomically via a temp file plus rename so a crash mid-write no longer leaves truncated JSON. `chat-history.ts` now throws on non-array `chat-messages.json` and pushes a `ChatHistoryEntry` with unreadable: true and lastPrompt: '(unreadable chat)' instead of hiding the chat, and `chat-history-screen.tsx` renders those entries as non-resumable but deletable rows showing a corrupted prompt placeholder. The `/new` command and `handleNewChat` callback now call `startNewChat()` to rotate the chat id before persisting, so the next save lands in a fresh directory rather than overwriting the previous conversation.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/write-file-atomic.ts` adds exported `writeFileAtomic`; `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` imports it and replaces both `fs.writeFileSync` calls in `saveChatState` with `writeFileAtomic`; `cli/src/utils/chat-history.ts` and `cli/src/components/chat-history-screen.tsx` add unreadable field handling so corrupt `chat-messages.json` is shown in `/history`; `cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts` and `cli/src/app.tsx` call `startNewChat()` in `/new` and `handleNewChat`

facts: Convert handleSteps function to string if present Convert handleSteps function to string if present, but keep the live function too: the stringified form of a bundled function can reference out-of-scope bundler helpers and fail the runtime's eval round-trip.

Live copy of handleSteps preserved for in-process execution (the string form of a bundled/minified function may not survive an eval round-trip). Never serialized: JSON.stringify drops function values. Typed loosely so the zod-inferred signature doesn't fight the StepHandler type.

Prefer the live function when present: the stringified form of a bundled function can reference out-of-scope bundler helpers (esbuild keepNames' `__name`, minified to a bare identifier), which makes the eval'd generator throw ReferenceError on its first step.

A ReferenceError from an eval'd handleSteps string almost always means the source was serialized from a bundled/minified function and references an out-of-scope bundler helper. Call it out so the failure is diagnosable from the message alone.
Live copy of handleSteps kept alongside its stringified form (see processedAgentDefinition below).

ai.title: handleStepsFn preserves live function across agent runtime
ai.summary: Added handleStepsFn to AgentTemplate and DynamicAgentTemplate schemas to retain the live function alongside its stringified form. The runtime now prefers handleStepsFn over eval'd strings to prevent ReferenceErrors from out-of-scope bundler helpers. Covers common types, agent-runtime, and SDK loaders. JSON serialization drops the function field automatically.

eli5.text: When you build a custom assistant workflow that runs special logic steps, the system now keeps that live step-function in memory next to the version it converts to text. This stops crashes where the text-only copy referenced code that wasn't available after being bundled and minified, which previously caused confusing 'ReferenceError' messages during in-process execution. Nothing changed for assistants saved to databases or disk, since the live function is automatically excluded during serialization.

facts: Checkpoint the turn to disk immediately so that killing the process (closed terminal, crash) can't lose the user's prompt, then keep the checkpoint fresh from SDK run-state snapshots while the run streams. The completion save below overwrites this with the final state.
Persist the last checkpoint plus the error banner so a restart after a failed run still shows this turn.
Stop exit-flushing this run's checkpoint; the final state (or last checkpoint, on error) has been saved above. Owner-guarded so an aborted run resolving late can't clear a newer run's provider.
Persist any in-flight chat state first (synchronous, best-effort) so closing the terminal or killing the process mid-run doesn't lose the turn.
Compact JSON: these files are rewritten on every checkpoint and grow to multiple MB; pretty-printing roughly doubles the write.
entries.title: CLI update: use-send-message
entries.summary: CLI, SDK changes across 7 file(s) (+558/−22).

ai.title: SDK checkpoints in-flight runs and CLI persists them to survive
ai.summary: `run()` in `sdk/src/run.ts` gains an `onStateSnapshot` hook fired once at start and every `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` (5000 ms) while in flight, yielding a `RunState` whose output carries `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE`; a `settled` guard and cleared `snapshotTimer` ensure snapshots never overwrite the final state, and an owner check stops a late snapshot from clobbering a newer run. The CLI wires that hook in `createRunConfig` and calls `saveChatState` from `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` at turn start, on each snapshot, and on error, so a killed terminal or crash keeps the last turn on disk, while `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` invokes `flushLiveChatState()` during process exit to persist any in-flight checkpoint. Supporting storage helpers in `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` (`setLiveChatStateProvider`, `clearLiveChatStateProvider`, `flushLiveChatState`, `setChatDirOverrideForTesting`) make the provider owner-guarded and best-effort, and `cli/src/utils/send-message-helpers.ts` adds `sanitizeRestoredMessages` to mark an interrupted `AI_MESSAGE_ID_PREFIX` AI response as complete with an interruption notice and cancel its running agent blocks.
ai.evidence: The diff adds an `onStateSnapshot` callback to `RunOptions` in `sdk/src/run.ts` (with `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000` and `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE` exports), threads it through `createRunConfig` in `cli/src/utils/create-run-config.ts`, and calls `saveChatState` from `useSendMessage` in `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` both at turn start and on each in-flight snapshot plus on error; `sdk/src/index.ts` now re-exports `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE`; `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` calls `flushLiveChatState()` in `cleanup()`; `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` adds `setLiveChatStateProvider`, `clearLiveChatStateProvider`, `flushLiveChatState`, and `setChatDirOverrideForTesting`; `cli/src/utils/send-message-helpers.ts` adds `AI_MESSAGE_ID_PREFIX`, `sanitizeRestoredMessages`, and imports `appendInterruptionNotice` and `markRunningAgentsAsCancelled`.
ai.migration: If you embed the CLI or SDK and relied on `run()` never calling back with a `RunState` before completion, you must now handle the optional `onStateSnapshot` snapshots in your host persistence layer.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the checkpoint snapshot is consumed by any downstream autosave or sync service beyond the CLI's `saveChatState`.

changes.what: `run()` accepts `onStateSnapshot` and emits a `RunState` snapshot immediately and every 5000 ms while in flight, stopping once the run settles.
`STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE` is now re-exported from the public SDK entry point.
`CreateRunConfigParams` and the returned config object now include `onStateSnapshot`.
Registers a live state provider, saves chat state at turn start and on each snapshot, saves the last checkpoint on error, and clears the provider in `finally`.
`cleanup()` now calls `flushLiveChatState()` first to persist any in-flight checkpoint before terminal reset.
Adds owner-guarded `setLiveChatStateProvider`/`clearLiveChatStateProvider`, best-effort `flushLiveChatState`, and a `setChatDirOverrideForTesting` escape hatch for tests.

facts: Resolve the Codebuff backend base URL at call time. Remote hosts that bundle the SDK (Convex Node actions, Next server routes) must not rely on the bundle-time value: esbuild can inline a dev-machine localhost URL that the remote runtime cannot reach. Deployment `process.env` wins when present.
entries.title: SDK update: client
entries.summary: SDK changes across 7 file(s) (+40/−16).

ai.title: SDK resolves backend URL at request time instead of bundle time
ai.summary: The SDK now resolves the Codebuff backend base URL via a new `getWebsiteUrl()` function in `sdk/src/constants.ts` instead of using the bundle-time `WEBSITE_URL` constant. `getWebsiteUrl()` checks `process.env['NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL']` or `process.env['CODEBUFF_APP_URL']` at call time, falling back to the value esbuild inlined at bundle time. The five internal consumers (CodebuffClient health check, Composio tool proxy, agent runtime client-env override, database fetch helpers, and model-provider backend URL builder) were switched to `getWebsiteUrl()`, so remote hosts that bundle the SDK can correct a dev-machine localhost URL from their own `process.env` instead of reaching an address they cannot reach.
ai.evidence: sdk/src/constants.ts replaces the constant `WEBSITE_URL = env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL` with a `getWebsiteUrl()` function that reads `process.env['NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL'] ?? process.env['CODEBUFF_APP_URL']` at call time, and the five call sites in sdk/src/client.ts, sdk/src/composio.ts, sdk/src/impl/database.ts, sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts, and sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts switch from `WEBSITE_URL` to `getWebsiteUrl()`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether existing callers of the deprecated `WEBSITE_URL` constant (e.g. cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts and cli/src/utils/codebuff-api.ts) will be migrated to `getWebsiteUrl()` in a follow-up.

facts: Keep the full transcript: this array is what saveChatState persists to chat-messages.json, so trimming here would permanently lose history. Rendering stays cheap because useChatMessages paginates what's shown.

Read committed state rather than saving inside a setMessages updater: the store uses immer, so the updater sees a draft proxy and JSON.stringify of the (unbounded) transcript through proxy traps is several times slower.

ai.title: Chat history lists via chat-meta sidecar
ai.summary: A new chat-meta.ts module adds CHAT_META_FILENAME ('chat-meta.json') and writeChatMeta/readChatMeta helpers, which saveChatState now invokes after writing chat-messages.json to emit a small sidecar with messageCount, firstPrompt, and the messages file's size/mtime, and clearChatState removes it. getAllChats in chat-history.ts prefers readChatMeta(info.chatPath) to avoid JSON.parsing every unbounded chat-messages.json when listing chats in /history, falling back to the full parse when the sidecar is missing, corrupt, or no longer matches the messages file.
